content:
Let \(x_1\le x_2\le\cdots\le x_{21}\) be the piece lengths, and suppose no two differ by at most \(m\). Then
\[
x_{i+1}-x_i>m\quad\Rightarrow\quad x_{21}>x_1+20m.
\]
Since \(x_{21}\le 3x_1\), we get
\[
x_1+20m<3x_1 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x_1>10m.
\]
Also,
\[
21=\sum x_i > 21x_1+210m,
\]
so
\[
x_1<1-10m.
\]
Thus \(10m<1-10m\), so \(m<\frac1{20}\). Therefore if \(m\ge \frac1{20}\), two pieces must differ by at most \(m\).

Sharpness: take lengths
\[
0.5,\ 0.55,\ 0.6,\ \ldots,\ 1.5.
\]
They sum to \(21\), satisfy max/min \(=3\), and no two differ by less than \(\frac1{20}\).

\[
\boxed{\frac1{20}}
\]
